text:
maria (secops): Heads up — red-team requested full session-level raw logs for vuln triage and an incident replay. Need clarity on retention, export path, and KMS protections. Are we comfortable providing raw session dumps?

asher (eng-sre): What’s the minimal artifact they actually need? full tty/session stdout or just auth + timeline metadata? we should avoid unnecessary PII.

jamie (platform): Prefer a timeboxed, tokenized snapshot served via SIEM export proxy. Give them a JIT-unwrapped artifact that auto-revokes. That avoids giving long-lived raw blobs. :thumbsup:

leo (infra): Two implementation options: (1) ephemeral S3 with CMK-encrypted objects + lifecycle delete at TTL, or (2) query-only role in Splunk that masks fields server-side. S3 gives a clean handoff but needs stricter onboarding.

maria (secops): If we go S3, we need a dedicated service account for red-team, an approval flow, and audit hooks for KMS decrypts. Can we reuse the existing ephemeral-escrow role or do we create a scoped variant?

asher (eng-sre): ephemeral-escrow currently scoped to oncall/forensics. We should create a "redteam-escrow" role with a narrower scope and an approval ticket requirement. Access should be timeboxed and auto-revoked.

jamie (platform): Example unwrap flow (for engineering reference):
```
# ops run to decrypt a snapshot (JIT)
aws s3 cp s3://ri-ephemeral-escrow/redteam/2024-04-01/snapshot.enc ./snapshot.enc
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://snapshot.enc --key-id alias/ri-logs --output text --query Plaintext | base64 --decode > snapshot.json
```
Keep the decryption in a controlled, logged environment.

audit-bot: Reminder — all KMS decrypt events are logged to CloudTrail and forwarded to SIEM. Those decrypt audit events are retained for 2 years by default.

leo (infra): Open question: export retention. Legal requests 90 days, forensics asks for 365 days for deeper investigations. I propose default 90d for red-team exports, with a documented exception process for 365d that requires a forensic/IR justification and legal signoff.

maria (secops): Agree on 90d default. Also require redaction of IP addresses, email/user IDs by default unless IR-approved. JIT unmasking should require a ticket and two approvers (sec + oncall). We should add a small playbook snippet for the unmask step.

asher (eng-sre): I'll draft a PR to add the "redteam-escrow" IAM role, lifecycle rules, and a TTL enforcement Lambda + automation to revoke access. Will also add a SIEM export transform to strip PII by default.

jamie (platform): Ping me on the PR for review. Also add a Console metric: "ephemeral-export-unwrap-count" and an alert when >3 unwraps/day for a single principal.

maria (secops): Created ticket SEC-4872 to track policy + PRs; linking legal for retention exception workflow: @legal-team. Thanks everyone — will capture playbook additions and circulate a short runbook for red-team onboarding. :white_check_mark:
